9. Navigation & Sidebar

9.1 How the Sidebar is Built

The sidebar is automatically generated from all active modules. The context processor navigation() in context_processors.py combines:

  • Base navigation from modules.json (Dashboard, fixed entries)
  • Module navigation from all found module.json files (via ModuleScanner)
  • System navigation (Admin Portal, Logout)

9.2 Multilingual Titles — titles_json

The sidebar displays module titles in the current language. This works via the titles field in module.json and the HTML attribute data-titles:

<!-- Generated by the _nav_link.html template: -->
<a href="/mein_modul/" class="nav-link"
   data-titles='{"de": "Mein Modul", "en": "My Module", "fr": "Mon Module"}'>
    <i class="bi bi-star"></i>
    <span class="nav-title">Mein Modul</span>
</a>

core-language.js reads all data-titles attributes when the language changes and updates the display automatically.

9.3 Highlighting the Active Module

The generic view automatically sets active_module in the context. The template uses it for the active CSS class:

<!-- In _nav_link.html -->
<a href="{{ module.route }}"
   class="nav-link {% if active_module == module.id %}active{% endif %}">
    ...
</a>

The active CSS class sets a darker background (--abcona-blue-dark) and white text.

9.4 Subpages in the Sidebar

Subpages appear as a submenu when the module is active. They are read from module.json → subpages:

<!-- Sidebar shows subpages when module is active: -->
{% if item.subpages and active_module == item.id %}
<div class="submenu ms-4">
    {% for subpage in item.subpages %}
    <a href="{{ subpage.route }}" class="nav-link subpage-link
        {% if active_subpage == subpage.id %}active{% endif %}">
        <i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short"></i>
        <span data-titles='{{ subpage.titles_json }}'>{{ subpage.title }}</span>
    </a>
    {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}

9.6 Controlling the Order

The order field in module.json determines the position in the sidebar (low = top):

Dashboard:        order: 10  ← fixed in modules.json
CV Upload:        order: 30
CV Editor:        order: 35
My Module:        order: 50  ← insert here
Documentation:    order: 20
Admin Portal:     order: 900 ← at the bottom

Administrators can also change the order via Admin → Modules — this change is saved in the database and overrides module.json.
